text:
alex_support: @acme-app-team thanks for filing. I see you've reported intermittent SSE disconnects from browsers (mostly Safari) and partial streaming responses. You mentioned spikes in token refresh errors and unexpected billing for duplicate partial outputs — correct?
acme-app-team: yes. Users get a bunch of short chunks, then connection drops. On reconnect we sometimes see repeated tokens / duplicated output and charges. Happening mostly on Safari 16/17 mobile and desktop. Works fine in Chrome. :frowning:
alex_support: ok — can you share a HAR or a minimal repro? Also which deployment: hosted or private? And are you using Authorization header or token-in-query for EventSource?
acme-app-team: hosted. We currently attach ?token=... to the url because browsers can't set headers on EventSource easily. Here's a small repro we used:

```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?token=eyJ...');
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = (e) => console.log('err', e);
```

We tested behind Cloudflare (our CDN) with standard caching rules. When the stream disconnects Safari never resumes body stream — the console shows "EventSource failed to connect" then we see a 304 from the CDN at the next request and tiny partial event. Curl works fine continuously.
alex_support: thanks. Maria from eng is looping in for root-cause.
maria_eng: looking. A few known vectors: Safari has stricter resource caching and revalidation behavior for long-lived connections; some CDNs will treat SSE endpoints as cacheable and return 304s on revalidate which can close the underlying connection or return an empty body. Also EventSource can't set Authorization headers, so tokens in URL + CDN cache will interact poorly if CDN is not varying on token. Two immediate suspects: 1) CDN returning 304 with no body on revalidation and 2) missing Vary headers (or CDN strip) so different tokens map to same cache key.
acme-app-team: we didn't set Vary: Authorization or Vary: Cookie. We thought query param would bypass cache.
maria_eng: Query params may not be sufficient depending on CDN config (Cloudflare can ignore querystring in some cache rules). Can you paste the response headers on a failing request? Particularly: Cache-Control, ETag, If-None-Match/304, Vary, Content-Encoding, Transfer-Encoding, and the status.
acme-app-team: pasted the failing response from Safari devtools:

```
HTTP/2 304 Not Modified
date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 12:00:05 GMT
cache-control: public, max-age=60
etag: "abc123"
age: 15
server: Cloudflare
cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED
x-edge: lhr
content-length: 0
```

There was no Vary header. The subsequent EventSource reconnect receives no body and Safari gives up.
maria_eng: that's the smoking gun. For SSE we must ensure the origin serves the stream as non-cacheable or at least the CDN is configured to bypass caching for the SSE path, and if you rely on token-in-query we must ensure the CDN includes the token in the cache key (or better: use Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache for SSE endpoints). When Cloudflare returns 304 with content-length 0 that will not satisfy EventSource's expectation of an open body and some browsers treat that as closed.
sam_oncall: FYI, we saw an incident last month similar where edge revalidation + SSE led to early EOF in Safari. Temporary mitigation was to set `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-store` and `Surrogate-Control: no-store` at the origin, and ensure ETag/If-None-Match not used for SSE route. Also recommended `Connection: keep-alive` but that's less reliable over HTTP/2. Also, ensure you are not using `Content-Encoding: gzip` + CDN recompression on streaming responses — that can force buffering.
acme-app-team: are there auth implications? We need short-lived tokens for security. We can't put long bearer tokens in URL.
maria_eng: security tradeoff: tokens in URL are logged in proxies; better is a cookie or use a session token via cookie (SameSite=None; Secure) for browsers. Alternatively use a custom proxy endpoint that accepts the Authorization header (XHR or fetch) and then proxies to the SSE endpoint server-side and streams to the client. That avoids putting tokens in the URL and allows CDN cache bypass.
acme-app-team: interesting. For now we need a quick mitigation because customers are complaining and we're getting duplicate charges.
alex_support: about billing: duplicates happen when reconnects cause the server to resume at last token and generate overlapping content. We can add a server-side dedupe by using idempotency keys or sequence ids from the stream (each message includes an event id). Do you include `id:` lines in SSE events?
acme-app-team: no, we're just streaming plain JSON lines.
maria_eng: add `id:` to SSE events and ensure clients send Last-Event-ID header on reconnect. Then the server can resume after the last acknowledged id and avoid duplication. Example SSE frame:

```
event: chunk
id: chunk-000123
data: {"text":"..."}

```

And on reconnect the browser will send `Last-Event-ID: chunk-000123` automatically if the EventSource received it, which the server can use. Note: Safari historically had spotty Last-Event-ID support for some polyfills; test.
acme-app-team: we also use a polyfill fallback for older Safari that implements EventSource via fetch/readableStream. Could that be worse?
maria_eng: yes: polyfills that use fetch and then buffer the whole response before streaming can interact badly with CDN 304 responses (fetch might treat 304 as terminal and polyfill fails). If your polyfill does a range request or uses XHR which triggers preflight, CORS preflight complexity increases.
acme-app-team: we saw CORS preflight errors in console occasionally: "Origin not allowed". Our SSE endpoint sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` but we sometimes need credentials.
maria_eng: if you need credentials (cookies) you must set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and echo the exact origin in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (can't use *). Also ensure `Vary: Origin` is present so CDN will cache per-origin correctly. For token-in-query you don't need credentials header but the CDN key is still a worry.
sam_oncall: concrete checklist we recommend:
- On the SSE route, set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` and `Surrogate-Control: no-store` on origin.
- Avoid ETag/If-None-Match/304 behavior for streams — disable revalidation for SSE path.
- Add `Vary: Origin` or `Vary: Authorization` as appropriate.
- Emit SSE `id:` fields for dedupe/resume semantics.
- Prefer cookie-based session or a server-side proxy to keep Authorization out of URL.
- If using polyfills, ensure they stream byte-for-byte and handle 304/empty-body explicitly; otherwise prefer native EventSource when available.
- If behind Cloudflare, use page rule / route to bypass cache for `/v1/streams` and disable Edge caching.

acme-app-team: we'll try disabling CDN caching for the endpoint and add SSE ids. Any quick diagnostic we should run to confirm 304 is the root cause?
maria_eng: reproduce with Safari devtools open and network tab. Trigger a reconnect and look for status 304 with content-length 0. Also run a tcpdump on origin (if private) or capture the raw request/response headers from origin logs to ensure revalidation is happening. You can also run this curl that simulates EventSource via chunked responses:

```
# server: stream a few lines with chunked encoding
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?token=TEST' --no-buffer
```

Then simulate Cloudflare by replaying via their edge if you can. Another useful test: attach a unique query param each connect (e.g., ?t=ts) and see if behavior changes — if it fixes it, cache key was the issue.
acme-app-team: thanks. We'll patch headers and try.
alex_support: I'll keep the case open. If you want an interim mitigation for billing, we can flag duplicate partial responses and issue a credit while we work. Would you like that?
acme-app-team: yes please, customers are upset.
alex_support: done — I've put a temporary credit and flagged account for engineering review escalation. Please update here when you have the headers change test results.
acme-app-team: will do. thanks all :pray:
deploy-bot: deploy completed to edge rule: /v1/streams bypass-cache -> true (job/5678) at 2026-03-15T12:06:29Z
